## Natural history notes

A large dragonfly characterized by its bright green thorax, long blue to greenish abdomen, clear wings, and strong, fast flight. In Florida, it is common around ponds, lakes, marshes, canals, wet prairies, ditches, and other freshwater wetlands with open water and emergent vegetation. Adults are powerful aerial predators that catch mosquitoes, flies, butterflies, and other flying insects, while the aquatic nymphs live among submerged vegetation and prey on small aquatic animals, including insect larvae and tadpoles.
